summary: Completes the installer-packaging plan (phases 4-7) on top of the already-shipped GoReleaser packaging: .github/workflows/main.yml now tags the commit v<mymatasan-version> and pushes it whenever a version bump changes the mymatasan app version, then calls a new reusable .github/workflows/release.yml (workflow_call + workflow_dispatch) that checks out the tag, runs GoReleaser, and extracts the newest CHANGELOG.md entry as the GitHub Release notes. mymatasan gained native Windows service support (infra/apphost/service_windows.go detects an SCM-launched process and runs it under svc.Run so services.msc Stop/Start triggers the same graceful shutdown as an OS signal; service_other.go is the no-op stub elsewhere; run.go's Run is now a thin platform dispatcher over the renamed runApp) plus a new Inno Setup Windows x64 installer (packaging/windows/mymatasan.iss) that installs to Program Files, keeps data in %ProgramData%\MyMataSan, and registers the service via sc.exe; release.yml gained a windows-installer job that builds and uploads it. The r450k marketing site added a live Download page (GET /api/downloads in the Cloudflare Worker reads the GitHub Releases API and edge-caches it) so releases surface without a site redeploy. mymatasan also gained an in-app AI runtime installer (new services/python_install.go, Settings -> AI -> Install AI runtime, GET/POST /api/settings/vision/ai-runtime/{status,install,install/status}) that downloads a self-contained astral python-build-standalone interpreter and pip-installs a GPU (CUDA) or CPU PyTorch build plus ultralytics for hosts with no usable Python at all, distinct from the existing Train-in-app 'Install GPU support' flow; the stock yolo11n.pt model is now bundled in every distribution channel (archives, .deb/.rpm, Windows installer) since only the heavy Python/torch runtime is fetched at install time. Finally, mymatasan gained in-app self-update (new services/update.go, Settings -> Version & Health -> Updates, GET /api/system/update, POST /api/system/update/{check,apply}): it checks GitHub Releases on a 6-hour schedule and on demand, and on installs that own their files (portable archive or the new Windows service installer) downloads the matching release archive, verifies its SHA-256 against checksums.txt, swaps the binary and static/ai assets into place, and restarts via the existing apphost.Restarter.
compatibility: Backward compatible for existing installs. Self-update is opt-out by install type rather than opt-in by config: it is automatically disabled (with in-panel guidance shown instead) via a new MYMATASAN_MANAGED env var set to 'package' by deploy/nfpm/mymatasan.service (upgrade via apt/dnf) and 'docker' by deploy/Dockerfile.release (pull + recreate the container); it is also disabled whenever the app's home directory isn't writable. No existing install is auto-updated without an explicit click on the new Update button, and the periodic GitHub check only ever reads release metadata (no download) until that click. The AI runtime installer is purely additive (a new optional download path alongside the existing setup.sh/setup.ps1 and 'Install GPU support' flows) and does not change the detector command for any install that hasn't run it. The Windows service install path is new and does not affect existing WinSW/NSSM-based Windows deployments (deploy/windows/mymatasan.winsw.xml is unchanged and still supported, e.g. for arm64). go.mod: golang.org/x/sys is promoted from an indirect to a direct dependency (needed by the new Windows service code); no version change.
